scenario: I work in customer service for a well-known retail giant. Today, a woman cut in front of the line, yelling at me that her Visa gift card, which was supposed to have $250, showed that it had no money on it. I told her there was nothing we could do, as Visa gift cards were out of our hands. I called a manager over to see if they had a possible solution. The woman kept shouting to my manager, saying that the cashier lied to her about it being active right away. I gathered from the ongoing conversation that the reason she was so desperate for this money was that she needed to pay a hospital bill for her child that was due today, but had no other money. Suddenly, it made sense why she was so frantic. She commented in a distressed tone, saying, “I wouldn't do this if I didn't need to!” If I ask my colleagues to give me some of their money, then the woman will be able to pay her bill. If I do not do this, her child will continue to suffer from a severe illness.
choice: I decide to ask my colleagues to give me some of their money
entities: i,the woman customer,the manager,the cashier who sold or discussed the gift card,the woman's child,other customers waiting in line
outcomes: My colleagues are interrupted and put under pressure to decide whether to give money
Contributing colleagues lose some of their own money

The woman's panic and distress lessen
